jobs.description: TL;DR This is a strategic operating role at the center of the company, reporting to the Head of Comms with a dotted line to our Cofounder and CEO. Your core job is making sure company leadership communication is clear, consistent, and compounding week after week as we scale. Around that core, you'll own the narrative, the moments, and the rhythms that keep a fast-growing global team aligned, and you'll run the programming lean, with AI doing the production work so your judgment goes where it matters most. The challenge: when a company doubles in a year across offices and oceans, shared context is the first thing that can break. The warmth of a small team gets diluted by process. Your job is to make sure none of that happens: that every person at Lovable knows where we're going, why, and their part in it, and hears it in a voice that still feels like us. WHY LOVABLE Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started. We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world. Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software. WHAT YOU'LL DO Be the CEO's communications partner. You'll help make sure what the company hears is consistent from week to week and compounds over quarters. And you'll be a genuine advisor: in the room early, pressure-testing how a decision will land before it's made, and holding a mirror up to leadership when the message and the reality drift apart. Own the company narrative and operating rhythm. You'll own recurring communications and the strategy behind them: the cadences that ensure every employee understands the strategy, the priorities, and the reasoning, not just the announcements. You'll connect the internal story to the external one so employees hear one narrative, whether it comes from the CEO, their manager, or the press. Run the moments that matter. Fundraises, strategy rollouts, reorgs and leadership changes, and other high-stakes comms. You'll partner with the Office of the CEO and leadership team to make sure these moments are planned, humane, and land without whiplash: employees hear things that affect them before any rumor mill does. Make our flagship forums worth showing up for. You'll own the editorial arc of company-wide all-hands, elevate the craft of everyone presenting, and keep these moments warm and personal as we grow past the size where that happens by default. Build an AI-native internal comms engine. You'll run programming that would traditionally take a team, alone, by defaulting to AI and Lovable itself for input gathering, chasing, aggregating, drafting, and measurement. Human judgment stays where it belongs: editorial calls, sensitive moments, and final approval. If you're still doing production work manually after three months, something has gone wrong. Raise the bar for how leaders communicate. At Lovable, functions own their own communication; internal comms is not a gatekeeper or a wordsmithing service. Your job is to make every leader and manager a better communicator: standards, tools, coaching, and talking points that equip managers to answer their teams' questions, because managers are the most trusted source most employees have. Measure understanding, not reach. You'll build lightweight feedback loops that test whether messages actually landed: can people explain the strategy in their own words, do they feel informed, are the whispers going quiet. And when the data says a message isn't landing because the substance is unclear, you'll feed that signal back to leadership rather than polishing the wording. WHO YOU ARE You're an operator and a general problem solver. You build scalable systems from scratch, you're rigorous and structured in how you work, and you have a track record of outstanding achievement in demanding environments. You may have grown up in communications, or you may come from chief of staff, founder's office, strategy, or consulting work with serious writing chops. You've earned the trust of a founder or CEO. You've been the person a chief executive relies on to sharpen their thinking and their words. You know how to advise without ego, push back with evidence, and keep confidence. Your judgment has been tested on sensitive, high-stakes communications. You write exceptionally. You know the difference between writing that informs and writing that aligns, and you can do both under deadline. You're AI-native to your core. You instinctively reach for AI to do the gathering and aggregating, and you're excited to build internal tools on Lovable itself. You see leverage where others see headcount requests. You read organizations well. You have a feel for the pulse of a company: what people are worried about, where context is missing, which message will land and which will breed cynicism. You listen as much as you broadcast, and you navigate cultural differences across our European and US offices with ease. You're discreet, low-ego, and steady. You'll sit closer to sensitive information than almost anyone in the company. You handle it with care, you share credit reflexively, and you stay calm when plans change on a Tuesday afternoon. WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW Strong partnership with our CEO is a big part of the job. Everything else is the platform it stands on. You'll be measured first on whether our CEO's communication is clearer, more consistent, and more trusted because you exist, and second on whether the company stays aligned as it scales. This function is lean by design. You will not be building a large internal comms team. You'll be building systems, AI workflows, and leader capability that make a large team unnecessary. If your instinct when work piles up is to hire, this role will frustrate you. If your instinct is to automate and equip, you'll thrive. Finally: joining Lovable Comms means you're deeply curious, data-driven, and not extremely precious about role boundaries. You find ways to work smarter with AI, to measure what matters, and to step into work that isn't technically "yours" when the moment calls for it.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the Role
We're looking for a Capabilities Researcher to join the team building Claude Security. In this role, you'll identify which security capabilities in frontier models are ready to build on, measure how well they perform, and work out how to make them useful to customers who are not security experts.
Frontier models have become substantially more capable at security work over recent generations, and they continue to improve with each release. That progress creates a set of practical questions: which capabilities are reliable enough to depend on, how they perform in realistic conditions, how they behave when an adversary is involved, and where their limits are. You'll be responsible for answering those questions through fast prototyping and rigorous evaluation, and your findings will shape what the team decides to build.
You'll also work on making those capabilities usable. Together with engineers on the team, you'll design the scaffolding, tooling, and defaults that let a strong model capability do useful work for a non-expert, and you'll stay involved as it becomes a product.
This is a research role on a product team, with a broad charge and real latitude in what you investigate. It suits someone who already has ideas about what AI should be able to do for security teams and wants the models, the time, and the engineering support to pursue them.
Responsibilities
Prototype rapidly to find define the AI frontier for cybersecurity work
Design evaluations that measure model performance on the work security teams actually do
Build the datasets, harnesses, and scoring those evaluations depend on
Engage with the cybersecurity community to help define where AI can make the most impact
Work with engineers and researchers to operationalize promising capabilities into something customers can rely on
Track how model capabilities for security are changing, and what that means for what we build next
Share findings that inform product direction, and partner with product leadership on priorities
You may be a good fit if you:
Have deep expertise in one or more security domains, such as vulnerability research, exploit development, reverse engineering, malware analysis, incident response, or offensive security
Have built AI-powered tools or capabilities for security work
Can get from an idea to a working prototype quickly, and abandon the ones that don't hold up
Are comfortable designing rigorous evaluations and interpreting the results honestly
Can write and communicate clearly about technical findings
Have 7+ years of experience in security research, security engineering, or a closely related field
Strong candidates may also have:
Published research, CTF results, CVEs, or open source security tooling
Experience with model evaluation, benchmarking, or red teaming
Experience building agentic applications
Familiarity with the safety considerations of AI in security contexts

회사 소개
쿠팡은 고객 감동 실현을 위해 존재합니다. 고객들이 "쿠팡 없이 그동안 어떻게 살았을까?" 라고 말할 때, 비로소 우리의 미션을 실현하고 있음을 알 수 있습니다. 고객들의 쇼핑과 식사, 생활 전반을 편하게 만들겠다는 유일한 집념으로 쿠팡은 수억 달러 규모의 이커머스 산업 전반의 혁신을 이끌고 있습니다. 쿠팡은 가장 빠르게 성장하는 이커머스 기업 중 하나로, 국내 커머스 업계에서의 독보적인 입지와, 고객 신뢰를 구축했습니다.
쿠팡은 스타트업 문화를 기반으로 한 글로벌 대형 상장사라고 자부합니다. 이것이 창립 당시의 기민함을 지하며, 신규 서비스를 끊임없이 출시하며 비즈니스를 확장해 나가는 우리의 성장 동력입니다. 쿠팡의 모든 임직원에게는 기업가 정신을 갖추고 새로운 혁신과 이니셔티브를 추진할 수 있는 기회가 주어집니다. 주저 없이 일에 뛰어들어 성과를 이루고자 하는 과감성이, 바로 쿠팡이 일하는 방식의 본질입니다. 쿠팡에서는 여러분 자신, 동료, 팀 그리고 회사 전체가 매일 성장하는 모습을 목격할 것입니다.
쿠팡의 모든 직원은 커머스의 미래를 만들겠다는 쿠팡의 미션에 진심입니다. 우리는 고객의 문제를 해결해 나가고, 전통적인 관념과 통념에 맞서며 실현 가능한 한계를 뛰어넘고 있습니다. 고가용성 (always-on) 과 최첨단의 앞선 기술 (high-tech), 초연결사회 (hyper-connected world) 에서의 놀라운 업무 경험을 원하신다면, 지금 바로 쿠팡에 합류하세요.
직무 소개
쿠팡 CS 조직에서 운영되는 AI 서비스의 품질을 책임지는 팀입니다.고객 경험에 직접 영향을 미치는 AI 산출물을 분석하고, 모델이 더 잘 동작할 수 있도록 개선 방향을 도출합니다. AI가 실제 서비스에서 어떻게 작동하는지 가장 가까이에서 이해하고 싶은 분께 적합한 포지션입니다.

jobs.description: Who are we? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Role Overview: As a Senior Research Engineer in our Safety team, you will play a key role in helping develop safer, more secure, and more reliable models. Your primary focus will be on building tools to enable easy data synthesis, analysis, and management, for complex combinations of real and synthetic data that is used in both model training and evaluation. You will own the cohesive vision of these tooling repositories. You will work closely with a team of research scientists and engineers to create tooling that enables tighter experimentation cycles, better data coverage of the real world, and more scientific rigour. You will have a lot of autonomy and need to be opinionated about what areas of the codebase need elegance and standards, and where that would be overengineering. You will be given high level experimental problems that need to be solved with efficient pipelines, and design and implement the solutions. Your data analysis will collaboratively feed into modelling decisions and experimentation. This role combines expertise in software engineering, statistics, and data science. If any of these topics sound interesting to you, we encourage you to apply. You will be working on the Modelling Safety and Trust team, so interest in these areas is a plus, but is not at all required. jobs.description: Our Purpose Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. Title and Summary Manager, Software Engineering (Sanction Service) Who is Mastercard? Mastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry. Our mission is to connect and power an inclusive, digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere by making transactions safe, simple, smart, and accessible. Using secure data and networks, partnerships and passion, our innovations and solutions help individuals, financial institutions, governments, and businesses realize their greatest potential. Our decency quotient, or DQ, drives our culture and everything we do inside and outside of our company. With connections across more than 210 countries and territories, we are building a sustainable world that unlocks priceless possibilities for all. Overview We are seeking a Manager, Software Engineering to lead the development and evolution of Mastercard's Sanctions Screening solutions. These solutions help financial institutions assess sanctions risk for payment transactions in real time, supporting regulatory compliance, risk management and secure global payment processing. This role is a hybrid of roughly 70% technical leadership and 30% people management. The successful candidate will remain deeply involved in system solutioning, technical designs, engineering execution and continuous improvement on AI assist software development workflow while also building, mentoring and leading a high-performing engineering team(of 7 people now) Key Responsibilities Technical Leadership (70%) • Own the technical direction, architecture and delivery strategy for the Sanctions Service platform, built in Java and C++ primarily. • Lead the design and implementation of scalable, reliable and secure software solutions meeting the common of enterprise standards. • Drive engineering excellence through design reviews, code quality, operational readiness and best practices. • Partner with Product, Architecture, Compliance and Operations teams to deliver business-critical capabilities. • Lead incident response, root cause analysis and continuous improvement initiatives. • Drive modernization efforts focused on scalability, resilience, cloud readiness and operational efficiency. • Serve as the senior technical escalation point for complex engineering and production challenges. AI & Agentic Engineering • Define and execute a strategy for adopting AI-assisted and agentic engineering capabilities across the software development lifecycle. • Leverage AI tools to improve software delivery, testing, operational support, documentation and developer productivity, focusing on achieve faster iteration on requirements gathering, specification elaboration and concepts validation • Identify opportunities to automate engineering workflows and reduce operational overhead. • Establish guardrails and governance for responsible AI adoption, including security, transparency and human oversight. • Foster a culture of experimentation and innovation while maintaining strong compliance and risk controls. People Leadership (30%) •Lead and develop a high-performing team of software engineers. • Conduct regular coaching, career development discussions and performance management activities. • Create an inclusive, accountable and psychologically safe team culture. • Partner with recruiting to attract, retain and develop top engineering talent. • Drive planning, prioritization and execution of team roadmaps and delivery commitments. • Establish clear goals, expectations and ownership across the team. Qualifications Required • Proven experience leading software engineering teams and delivering large-scale enterprise software solutions. • Strong technical background with experience designing distributed, highly available systems. • Demonstrated ability to balance hands-on technical leadership with people management responsibilities. • Experience managing product roadmaps, business priorities, engineering deliverables and technical risks. • Strong communication, collaboration and stakeholder-management skills. • Experience with Agile software development and modern engineering practices. • Passion for mentoring engineers and building high-performing teams. Preferred • Experience in payments, financial services, compliance, fraud, sanctions screening or risk management will be a great bonus. • Experience leveraging AI-assisted development tools, agentic workflows or intelligent automation solutions. • Experience operating services in regulated, security-sensitive environments. • Knowledge of cloud platforms, DevOps practices and modern observability tooling. • Bachelor’s in computer science, Engineering or a related discipline. What Success Looks Like • A high-performing engineering team with strong engagement, accountability and technical excellence. • Predictable delivery of secure, scalable and reliable Sanctions Service capabilities. • Successful adoption of AI-enabled engineering practices proven by industries that improve productivity and delivery quality. • Measurable improvements in platform resilience, operational efficiency and customer outcomes. • Strong alignment across engineering, product, compliance and operational stakeholders. Mastercard is a merit-based, inclusive, equal opportunity employer that considers applicants without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disabled or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Do not include any medical or health information in this email. The Reasonable Accommodations team will respond to your email promptly. Corporate Security Responsibility All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must: Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices; Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed; Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.
